title: បាន — the most misunderstood word
goal: Master បាន, a word that pops up everywhere and that almost every beginner mistakes for a past-tense marker — which it isn't. This is the hardest unit in the book.
bekal: recognize the four jobs បាន does in a sentence
use … បានទេ? to ask permission
use បាន + a length of time to say how long
talk about the past without បាន at all
tell បាន, ចេះ, and អាច apart

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Renting a motorbike
dialogs.intro: Ani rents a motorbike for a month. Count how many times បាន appears in this dialogue — and notice that its meaning changes almost every time. The last line sums up the whole unit in one sentence.

lines.text: [ជួល|chuèl] [ម៉ូតូ|mou-tou] [មួយ|muèy] [ខែ|khae] [បាន|baan] [ទេ|té] [ចាស|chaah]?

grammars.title: ⚠️ បាន is NOT a past-tense marker
body: Almost every textbook calls បាន a "past marker", and so almost every beginner sticks it onto every sentence about yesterday. The result sounds odd — like someone stressing something for no reason. The basic meaning of បាន is **"to get"**, and all its other jobs grow out of that.

head: Job
Example
Say it
Meaning
rows: ខ្ញុំ**បាន**លុយ
ខ្ញុំមក**បាន**ពីរសប្តាហ៍
managed to, got to (BEFORE the verb)
ខ្ញុំ**បាន**ជួបគាត់

after: ⚠️ **To talk about the past, Khmer needs nothing at all.** ម្សិលមិញខ្ញុំទៅផ្សារ ("yesterday I go market") is perfect as it is. A time word — ម្សិលមិញ, ឆ្នាំមុន, ពេលនោះ — is enough.

So when does បាន really go before a verb? When you want to stress that something **actually happened**, often because it was in doubt: ខ្ញុំបានទៅមែន ("I did go, really"). Think of English "I **did** go" or "I **got to** go" — that's the right flavor.
**Rule of thumb for your first year: when in doubt, leave បាន out.** A sentence without បាន is almost never wrong; a sentence with an unnecessary បាន always sounds odd.

grammars.title: … បានទេ? — how to ask permission for anything
body: បាន placed **after** a verb means "may" or "can". This is the most useful pattern in this unit, maybe in the whole book: one mold that holds hundreds of requests.

head: English
Khmer
Say it
rows: ថតរូបបានទេ?
បង់ដុល្លារបានទេ?
អង្គុយទីនេះបានទេ?

after: The "yes" answer is just បាន on its own; the "no" answer is មិនបានទេ or អត់បានទេ. ⚠️ Note that បានទេ? here is **not** a question about the past at all — it's about permission, right now.

grammars.title: បាន, ចេះ, and អាច — three kinds of "can"
body: English uses one word, "can", for three things that Khmer keeps apart. Mixing them up won't make you incomprehensible, but it will make your sentences sound translated.

head: Word
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: can because you've **learned** it, know how
ចេះបើកម៉ូតូ — can ride a motorbike
អាចទៅបាន — can go (have time, are able)
ចូលបាន — may come in

after: ⚠️ Compare these two sentences: ខ្ញុំចេះហែលទឹក means "I can swim" (I've learned to swim). ខ្ញុំអាចហែលទឹកបាន means "I'm able to swim" (say, because the water is calm or my leg has healed). Someone who never learned to swim could say the second one in a pool half a meter deep.
For languages: **ចេះភាសាខ្មែរ** = to know Khmer. This is the right word, and the one Cambodians always use when they praise you.

sections.title: Telling the past with no marker at all

blocks.text: Since Khmer doesn't change its verbs and doesn't require បាន, the whole job of time falls on **time words**. Memorize this list and you can already talk about the past without a single grammar marker.

head: Khmer
Say it
English
rows: អាទិត្យមុន

blocks.text: ⚠️ Notice the ending **មិញ** (*meñ*) that keeps coming back: ម្សិលមិញ, យប់មិញ, ព្រឹកមិញ, អំបាញ់មិញ. មិញ means "just past", and attaching it is the shortest way to talk about the recent past. One ending, four words.
How long — the pattern បាន + length of time

head: English
Khmer
Say it
rows: បានប៉ុន្មានហើយ?
បានពីរសប្តាហ៍ហើយ
I've been in Cambodia for three months.
ខ្ញុំនៅកម្ពុជាបានបីខែហើយ
*khnyom neuw kam-pu-chiè baan bey khae haeuy*
She has worked here for ten years.
គាត់ធ្វើការទីនេះបានដប់ឆ្នាំហើយ
*koat thweu-kaa tii-nih baan dop chhnam haeuy*

blocks.title: Summary to take with you
items: **Talking about yesterday?** Say when, and don't touch the verb. ម្សិលមិញខ្ញុំទៅផ្សារ.
**Asking permission?** Add បានទេ? at the end. ចូលបានទេ?
**Saying how long?** បាន + number + unit + ហើយ. បានពីរឆ្នាំហើយ.
**Not sure?** Drop បាន. Your sentence will still be right.
